In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of c-Raf by the 14-3-zeta isoform.
the regulation of the protein kinase c-Ras and the identification of its regulatory proteins.
the interaction of 14- 3-3 protein isoforms and the serine/threonin protein kinase c-Ras.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 14-3 protein family is involved in the control of c-Raf signalling by a complex mechanism of interaction and regulation.
the 14-3-zeta protein binds to the carboxyl terminus of c-RAF in an unphosphorylable state and to the amino termini of c-RAFs in a phosphorylable state.
14- 3-3 zetas binding to the amino termini of c-Raf isoforms may be a regulatory step of c-Raf kinase activity, which is modulated by Ras and/or by phosphorylation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
14- 3-3 z is displaced from the c-Raf- 1 N terminus by binding of activated ras to c-Raf.
activated Ras displaces 1 of 2 14-3-zeta binding sites of c-Raf, but not the second binding site.
activated Ras is able to displace 14-3 from the amino termini of c-Raf, which is a prerequisite for c-Raf activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
14- 3-3 zetas binding to the carboxyl terminus of c- Raf-1 is not affected by the presence of Ras.
the binding site for activated Ras and the binding site for 14-3 zeta overlap in the amino terminus.
the binding of 14 3-3 z to the amino termini of Raf-1 is regulated by Ras.
